Sample.Title: MCF7_ChIP-seq input_DMSO 30 min_set 1

Channel.Treatment-Protocol: MCF-7 cells maintained in phenol red-free MEM supplimented with 5% charcoal-dextran treated calf serum, 2mM GlutaMax, 100u/mL penicillin-streptomycin, and 25ug/mL gentamicin were seeded such that cells will bet at 70 to 80% confluency at the time of experimentation. Cells were treated with the indicated concentrations of E2 for 30 min., after which they were fixed with 1% formaldahyde for 10 mins at 37C before quencing with glycine at a final concentration of 125 mM. Fixed cells were snap frozen and stored at -80C until use.
Channel.Growth-Protocol: MCF-7 human epithelia cells from breast adenocarsinoma cells from American Type Cell Culture (ATCC) were maintained in MEM supplemented with 5% calf serum, 2mM GlutaMax, 100u/mL penicillin-streptomycin, and 25ug/mL gentamicin. MCF-7 cells were maintained in phenol red-free MEM supplimented with 5% charcoal-dextrantreated calf serum, 2mM GlutaMax, 100u/mL penicillin-streptomycin, and 25ug/mL gentamicin for at least 3 days prior to experimentation.
Channel.Extract-Protocol: Nuclei were first extracted by inclubation in Farmham lysis buffer followed by centrifugation. Nuclei were then lysed in lysis buffer containing SDS, and sonicated for 8 cycles (30on/off) in a Dyagenode pico sonication device. Shear chromatin was cleared by incubation in dynabeads, protein concnetration measured, and at least 0.5 mg of material used for ChIP assays using the indicated antibody as described. Final ChIP'ed DNA was purified by phenol chloroform extraction followed by ethanol precipitation. ChIP-seq libraries were generated as previously described (Judd J, et al., BioRxiv 2020). Libraries were generated from ChIP'ed DNA or input as described, and subjected to quality control analyses, such as optimizing the number of PCR cycles required to amplify each set of libraries, adapter cleanup by SPRI-bead purification, quantifying the final library yield by Qubit fluorometer (Invitrogen, Q32851), and checking the size distribution of the final library by DNA ScreenTape system (Agilent Technologies, G2964AA, 5067–5584, and 5067–5603). The libraries were barcoded with indices as described using Illumina indexed barcodes and sequenced using Illumina NextSeq (2000) by 100 bp single-end sequencing.

Series.Title: Dose-dependent Effects of Estrogen on Genomic Regulation in Breast Cancer Cells [ChIP-seq]
Series.Summary: Estrogen is the primary mitogen for ER+ BC cells. However, most studies prior to this examining the genomic effects of E2-regulated signaling in cell-based assays used supraphysiological levels of hormone. While this has allowed us to understand the extremes of E2 signaling, it has limited our ability to examine cellular functions which operate at lower hormone concentrations. In particular, the genomic actions of ligand-bound ERa through transcriptional enhancer formation and function are not understood at physiological E2 doses. Here, we use an integrated genomic approach with RNA-seq, PRO-seq, ChIP-seq, and ATAC-seq to identify gene sets that express preferentially at either picomolar or nanomolar concentrations of E2. Expression of these genes is regulated mainly at the transcriptional level and is associated with distinct enhancer features, including chromatin accessibility and H3K27ac enrichment, as well as differential binding of FOXA1 and GATA3 co-transcription factors.
Series.Overall-Design: ERa, H3K27ac, FOXA1, or GATA3 ChIP-seq of MCF-7 cells treated with a range of E2 concentrations (veh., 10 pM, 100 pM, 1 nM, 10 nM).
Series.Type: Genome binding/occupancy profiling by high throughput sequencing
